comments.text: The depth table, built at the start by depth_init ($24BC) over whatever the file holds here: 64 rows, one for each depth from the thrower (row 0) to the far end (row 63), of 64 bytes each. Row d, column c holds 2c x (128 - d) / 128, the distance from the middle of a view at which a bolt c units off centre is drawn at depth d, so the bolts shrink towards the middle as they fly away.

Psychic Judo's entry, jumped to by the resident event loader at $0970: silences the SID (sid_init $7254) and shows the event's title screen through the resident $C540 (A = 3).

Banks the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out, points the NMI vector at nmi_rti ($6D35) and the IRQ vector at irq_entry ($255D), turns on the raster interrupt, picks video bank 1 with the screen at $4000 and the character set at $4800 in multicolour, builds the opponents' figures ($300E), draws the screen ($2624), clears the round lamps ($6C99), draws the arena into both views ($26EA), builds the depth table ($24BC), draws the bars, clock, round wins and figures, blacks the sprites and puts sprites 4 to 7 (the shadows) behind the picture.
Picks video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) in CIA 2, the screen at $4000 and the character set at $4800, then turns on multicolour text.

The top of a match: clears both players' match times ($73CD-$73D2) and round wins, stops play ($1E8B), empties the bars, sets the clock to 0.00, plays effect 7 and draws the figures. Asks for fire ($1E5B, "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY"); with no press it plays the demo, otherwise asks who is playing ($3D40).

The top of each round: resets both players ($1ECA: full reserves, no bolts or shields), sets the clock to 60.00, plays effect 7, shows "SECONDS OUT" and "GAME ON" fifty frames apart, plays effect 1 and starts the clock and play.

Once a frame: in the demo, a fire press starts a match ($1CC4). Otherwise reads the controls ($3EB6), draws the clock, runs both players ($1F0D, $2011), draws the figures and the bars; ends the round when a player's reserve runs out ($1E95, $1E96) or the clock reaches zero ($1E8D).

The clock ran out: plays effect 1, stops play, shows "TIMEOUT ROUND OVER" (or "HEY  ARE YOU GUYS GONNA PLAY OR WHAT" when both reserves are still full), then "ROUND DRAWN" and "REPLAY ROUND", and replays the round.

A reserve ran out: the player with more energy left wins the round (equal reserves draw it: "ROUND DRAWN", "REPLAY ROUND", $1E09). Adds one to the winner's round wins, puts their number into "PLAYER   WINS ROUND" (the byte at $3D33, $5C or $5D, which the message line draws as character $A7 or $A8), adds the round's time to their match time ($73D5), plays effect 7 and draws the round wins; three wins take the match ("PLAYER ONE WINS MATCH" or "PLAYER TWO WINS MATCH"), with the time kept for the records ($7363), and a new match starts.
Shows "ROUND DRAWN" and "REPLAY ROUND", a hundred frames each, and replays the round.
Shows "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY" and waits 256 frames for a fire press; with one, plays effect 5, without one shows "DEMO MODE" and sets the demo ($1E8A = $FF, players 0).

The game's state: wait_start's count ($1E88), the player count ($1E89: 2 two players, 1 the computer plays player one, 0 the demo), the demo flag ($1E8A), play stopped ($1E8B), the timers held ($1E8C), the round timed out ($1E8D) and the clock running ($1E8E).

Per player: the computer's delay before its next move ($1EAA), the delay it reloads ($1EAC), the charging time left ($1EAE), the forced throw flag ($1EB0) and the computer's state ($1EB2: 0 idle, 1 deciding, 2 charging, 3 steering, 4 defending, 5 throwing).

Fills both reserves ($2F) and clears the bolts, shields, flashes and computer states.

Player one's turn. With a bolt flying, steers it ($1F98): the stick moves it up, down, left or right at speed 1, and its shape follows (table $2005). With a bolt charging, a fire release, or the charging time running out ($1EB0), throws it (state $C0, effect 6). With no bolt, while player two has one (charging or flying) the stick raises a shield ($1F61, from shield_dirs); otherwise, with at least 2 in the reserve, a new fire press starts a bolt: it appears in front of the player (across $1E, depth 2, height $1E), moving away at speed 1, with 1 taken from the reserve and given to the bolt, and effect 8.
The bolt's shape offset for each stick direction, by the bits of the direction steered (up, down, left, right).
player_one's work byte.
Player two's turn, the same as player_one with the depth reversed: the new bolt starts at depth $3D and comes towards player one.
Player two's shape offsets, with left and right swapped.
player_two's work byte.
The stick positions that raise a shield (a 1 bit for each direction or fire held), matched by shield_zones.

The shield each stick position raises, a bit for each of the six body zones ($01 top left, $02 top right, $04 middle left, $08 middle right, $10 bottom left, $20 bottom right): up or down alone none; left or right the middle zone on that side; a diagonal the top or bottom zone on that side; fire and up both top zones, fire and down both bottom, fire alone both middle, fire and left the left column, fire and right the right column.
0 or 5, added to the bolts' shapes and toggled with their colour, so they flicker.

The bolts' shapes, eight depth bands for each steering direction.

Sets the shapes of player one's bolt in player one's view (sprite 0) and its shadow (sprite 4), from its depth band and steering.

Sets the shapes of player two's bolt in player one's view (sprites 1 and 5), from its depth band seen from the far end.
Sets the shapes of player two's bolt in player two's own view (sprites 3 and 7), from its depth band counted from player two's end and its steering.
Projects a point: X across (0 to $3F) and Y depth (0 to $3F) give the screen offset $40 plus or minus the depth table's entry for that depth and distance from the middle.

Once a frame, moves each flying bolt by its speeds on the three axes. A bolt that reaches either end of an axis (under 3 or $3D and over) stops: its sprites are hidden, both computer players go back to idle at once, and it is judged where it stopped (player one's at $2B37, player two's at $2BB2).

The band handler at line 256, once a frame: checks RUN/STOP ($6D36), sets a light grey background, runs the sound ($71B5) and the cursor flash ($2F54); while play runs, moves the bolts, sets their shapes and places all eight sprites, runs the clock ($36A8) and, unless held, the timers ($3567).
Ends every band handler: acknowledges the interrupt, moves to the next of five bands, sets its raster line and the handler the next interrupt jumps to, restores A, X and Y and returns.

Colours the screen light blue, copies the picture at $36D5 to the screen, clears the message line in white and sets the multicolour colours (light blue and black).

Player one's bolt has stopped. Only at the far end (depth $3D) can it reach player two: its place (across / 4, height / 4) on the 16 x 16 body map ($2C30) says whether it reaches the body and which zone. A miss plays effect 1. A shielded zone catches it: player two's reserve gains the bolt's energy (at most $2F), with effect 2. An open zone is a hit: player two loses one and a half times the bolt's energy, and an empty reserve ends the round ($1E96), with effect 3.
Player two's bolt stopped: the same at player one's end (depth 2).
Looks up cell X, Y of the 16 x 16 body map: carry clear when the cell is not the body; otherwise carry set, with A = 0 when its zone is in shield A and 1 when it is not.

Draws a reserve bar of six characters at ($11): A is the energy, at most $2F; full cells $66, a part cell $5F plus the remainder, empty cells $6E. Colours it green, or the flashing low colour under $0C.

The per-frame timers: every 3 frames cycles the four bolt sprites' colours and flickers their shapes; every 12 frames switches the low bars' colour; every 5 frames, for a charging bolt, moves 1 from the reserve to the bolt (at most $0C), until the charging time runs out; every 25 frames charges each raised shield 1 for every zone it covers, dropping it when the reserve runs out; counts down the computer's delays and $6B5C, which player two's charging sets to 500.

The computer's controls for player A (0 or 1): while its delay runs ($1EAA) it repeats its last controls; then it runs the routine for its state ($1EB2) from $6928, which returns the controls and sets the next delay.

The computer's state routines: 0 idle ($6B07), 1 deciding ($6941), 2 charging ($696B), 3 steering ($699E), 4 defending ($6A48), 5 throwing ($697A).
The state routines' addresses, high bytes, read with the low bytes at $6928.
When the computer is still waiting out its delay, it returns last frame's controls ($1E97), so it keeps doing what it was doing.
Sets the computer's delay from its reload value ($1EAC) and returns the controls in A.
State 1: if the opponent is not charging or throwing, holds fire to charge a bolt (state 2, for a random 7 to 31 frames); otherwise waits to defend (state 4).
State 2: releases fire, throwing the bolt (state 5, 10 frames).
State 5: steers the new bolt diagonally at random for 5 frames, then goes on steering (state 3).
State 3: one time in sixteen steers at random again; otherwise steers towards a part of the opponent left open, across ($69D8) and up or down ($6A0B), in a random order.
Steers across: away from the side whose zones the opponent's shield covers (the left column $15, the right $2A).
Steers up or down by the bolt's height: towards the top, middle or bottom zones, whichever band the bolt is in and the opponent leaves open.

State 4: while the opponent's bolt is in the far half it does nothing; nearer, it raises a shield on the bolt's side (left or right of the middle) and at its height, sometimes with fire for a pair of zones.

State 0: the computer as player one holds back while $6B5C runs and its reserve is lower than the other's; otherwise, unless its reserve is under 10, it waits a random 20 to 35 frames and starts deciding (state 1).
